stemMd: What gives the biography its unsettling authority is its author's refusal to ______ her subject's cruelty: every episode is set down in full, with never a hint that circumstances made any of it forgivable.
instructionsMd: Select exactly two answer choices that, when used to complete the sentence, fit the meaning of the sentence as a whole and produce completed sentences alike in meaning. There is no credit for a partially correct selection.
explanationMd:
This item has a trap built into its grammar: the blank sits after **"refusal to,"** so the word you choose names something the biographer does **not** do. Fill the blank with the wrong polarity and the sentence reverses.

**Step 1 — read what she does do.** After the colon: "every episode is set down in full." She reports the cruelty completely and openly. So the blank cannot be any verb meaning *report*, *reveal* or *list* — she refuses none of those; she does them.

**Step 2 — read the second half of the evidence.** "with never a hint that circumstances made any of it forgivable." *That* is what she withholds: she never softens the record, never offers a mitigating gloss. The blank must therefore mean *to make an offence seem less serious*.

**Step 3 — find the pair.** *Extenuate* means to represent a fault as less blameworthy, usually by pointing to circumstances — which is precisely the move the sentence says she never makes. *Palliate* means to make an offence appear less grave, to gloss over. The two completed sentences say the same thing: she will not soften her subject's cruelty. **The answer is extenuate and palliate.**

**How to check:** substitute each candidate and ask whether the resulting sentence agrees with the clause after the colon. "Refusal to disclose ... every episode is set down in full" is a flat contradiction, and the same contradiction appears with *itemize*, *publicize* and *recount*. Only the softening words survive. As a second check, confirm the pair really is a pair: *extenuate* and *palliate* are close enough that a reader would not notice which the author had used. That interchangeability, not mere plausibility, is what Sentence Equivalence asks for — and it is why four report-words, however tempting they look as a cluster, cannot supply the answer.

distractorRationale.f: "Disclose" means to reveal what was hidden, but the clause after the colon states that every episode is set down in full. A refusal to disclose would make the biographer a concealer, contradicting the sentence's own evidence.
distractorRationale.d: "Itemize" means to set out point by point, which is close to what "every episode is set down in full" describes her as doing. Saying she refuses to itemize turns the sentence against itself.
distractorRationale.b: "Publicize" means to bring to public notice. Publishing the episodes in a biography is doing exactly that, so a refusal to publicize cannot be the source of the book's authority; the word also carries a promotional sense foreign to the sentence.
distractorRationale.e: "Recount" means to narrate. It is the most natural-sounding of the report words and pairs neatly with "disclose" or "itemize", but the same objection kills it: the biographer does recount the episodes, in full, so she refuses nothing of the kind.

The six choices are: A, disclose. B, extenuate. C, itemize. D, palliate. E, publicize. F, recount. Select exactly two choices that fit the sentence and produce completed sentences alike in meaning. There is no credit for a partially correct selection.

provenance.notes: Original Sentence Equivalence item. Six choices, exactly two correct, scored all-or-nothing. Four report-family decoys (disclose, itemize, publicize, recount) are ruled out by the clause 'every episode is set down in full', which was written specifically to close them off; the mitigating clause 'never a hint that circumstances made any of it forgivable' fixes the required meaning. independentSolve.workingNotes: The colon explains the blank: 'never a hint that circumstances made any of it forgivable' means she refuses to excuse or soften the cruelty, so extenuate and palliate, which are close synonyms in this sense. Disclose, itemize, recount and publicize are ruled out by the other half of the colon - 'every episode is set down in full' means she does disclose and recount - and although those four are near-synonyms of one another, they produce sentences that contradict the given evidence.

review.notes: Uniqueness argument: extenuate and palliate are the only pair meaning 'to make an offence seem less serious', which is the meaning the second half of the post-colon clause demands. The four report-family words are each contradicted by 'every episode is set down in full'. A candidate such as 'condemn' was considered and deliberately excluded, because a plain unglossed record could arguably be described as withholding condemnation, which would have created a second defensible reading. sectionKey is verbal-1 because the exam config attaches the verbal-sentence-equivalence domain to verbal-1 and the loader errors on a domain/section mismatch; verbal-2 draws from the verbal-1 pool via poolSectionKey.
